facts.content: Patient had a C-section 4 weeks ago.
Patient took Codeine, last dose around 1 week ago.
Patient is allergic to Ibuprofen, reaction unspecified.
Patient's mother has a history of leg clots.
Patient lives with a partner and cares for a 4-week-old infant.
facts.source_text: SH: Lives with partner; caring for 4-wk-old infant

facts.content: Patient was alone at the time of the call.
facts.source_text: SH: alone at time of call

facts.content: Patient has a radial pulse of 30 beats per 15 seconds, approximately 120 bpm, indicating tachycardia.
facts.source_text: Radial pulse: 30 beats/15 s (~120 bpm) → tachycardic

facts.content: Acute shortness of breath and tachycardia 4 weeks postpartum rule out pulmonary embolism.
facts.source_text: Acute SOB + tachycardia, 4 wks postpartum → r/o pulmonary embolism

facts.content: Patient is in post-operative status 4 weeks after a C-section.
Palpitations likely secondary to anxiety or pain related to the suspected pulmonary embolism.
Patient is advised to seek immediate emergency department evaluation and discusses transport options. Opts to self-drive with infant supplies.
facts.source_text: Advise immediate ED evaluation; discuss ambulance vs self-transport → pt opts to self-drive promptly with infant supplies

facts.content: Patient is to hold Codeine until further assessment.
Educate the patient about increased clot risk postpartum and explain need for imaging or anticoagulation if pulmonary embolism is confirmed.
facts.source_text: Educate re ↑ clot risk postpartum; explain need for imaging/anticoag if PE confirmed

facts.content: Patient is encouraged to seek help sooner if symptoms worsen while en route and to call emergency services if deterioration occurs.
facts.source_text: Encourage to seek help sooner if worsening en route; call emergency services if deterioration
